debate_title: Compute governance as a lever for AI safety: export contr...

conflicts.point: Whether physical infrastructure metrics like data-center power consumption and semiconductor shipments provide a reliable, enforceable anchor that cannot be circumvented by algorithmic efficiency gains and decentralized commodity hardware.

positions.stance: Training frontier neural networks requires massive, synchronized physical compute infrastructure drawing megawatt-scale continuous power that leaves an unmistakable supply-chain and thermodynamic audit trail.
Algorithmic efficiency gains and modular distillation allow developers to achieve frontier performance on decentralized commodity hardware well below statutory audit thresholds.

conflicts.point: Whether the Bureau of Industry and Security compute thresholds primarily function as a vital national security firewall against irreversible dual-use risks or as a protectionist capture mechanism that stifles domestic innovation.

positions.stance: Preventing unconstrained frontier AI scaling and irreversible catastrophic safety risks outweighs the economic friction and compliance costs imposed on domestic hardware manufacturers.
Avoiding the moral and economic harm of regulatory delays on medical and technological progress takes precedence over speculative, unmanageable systemic safety risks.

verdicts.conflict: Whether physical infrastructure metrics provide a reliable anchor or can be circumvented by algorithmic efficiency gains and decentralized hardware.
verdicts.rationale: Training frontier models requires massive, synchronized clusters drawing megawatt-scale power that creates a verifiable physical audit trail. The safetyist position relies on concrete thermodynamic constraints, whereas the counterargument of widespread decentralization remains largely theoretical for frontier-scale runs.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Documented evidence of multiple frontier-grade training runs completed entirely on decentralized consumer hardware below the statutory compute threshold.

verdicts.conflict: Whether Bureau of Industry and Security compute thresholds function as a vital national security firewall or a protectionist capture mechanism.
verdicts.rationale: Export control frameworks impose documented compliance overhead and legal costs that disproportionately burden emerging domestic startups compared to incumbent technology firms. The accelerationist position accounts for the direct economic friction of regulation on market participants with greater empirical grounding in current trade data.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical proof that tiered compliance exemptions successfully eliminate startup friction without enabling foreign or domestic circumvention.
